083437776a13.text: New teaching implementation using RFC 6238’s public test key. No account secrets. No REA calls in your browser.

4a51d9174aa2.text: 02. Find the time-based method in the APK

63958abe09f3.text: inspected Aegis v3.4.3 with REA 6.1.0. To follow its trail,

9a473120e000.text: , record its hash and search for the TOTP class. Commands below use REA 6.4.0.

Follow its calls through counter encoding, HMAC, truncation and decimal formatting. Recover default period, hash and digit count. Cite each method inspected and distinguish defaults from per-account settings. Do not execute the APK.

53b18a5f10f5.text: Finding a division by 30 is only the start. The upstream report connects five stages: floor time into a counter; encode that counter in eight big-endian bytes; compute HMAC with the key; select a positive 31-bit value from the hash; reduce it to six digits and retain leading zeroes.

981a19f3aa25.text: Follow returned method calls rather than relying on familiar source names. In the inspected release, optimization placed generator helpers under

9a59af84d3bd.text: . The report also distinguishes default SHA-1, six digits and 30 seconds from account-specific settings.

891dffaa11a1.text: Implement the recovered behavior independently, then use public reference vectors. Test just before and after a time boundary, a leading-zero result and both six- and eight-digit output. Adjacent windows are not mathematically guaranteed to have different codes, even though this example does.

1791d8e45888.text: Write a small independent TOTP implementation for this recovered behavior. Use only RFC 6238 public test keys. Verify all six SHA-1 reference timestamps at eight digits and their six-digit remainders. Test the 29/30 and 59/60 boundaries and preserve leading zeroes. Explain any difference from the inspected method; do not claim to rebuild the vault or Android app.

2f9d1de962d2.text: Use REA to investigate Windows Calculator’s percent key. Compare addition and multiplication, inspect the branch, and test a two-operand demo.

1a546ec7585f.text: The launcher may not contain the calculation

3fd1278e2734.text: Test the intermediate value, not only the answer

a17b04f5d5ce.text: 01. Try it before taking it apart

80cce7feabf2.text: Leave the numbers at 200 and 10. Press Apply %: the second number becomes 20. Press Then = to get 220. Switch to multiplication and repeat: the second number becomes 0.1, and the final result is 20.

d5525ff59c6e.text: Press % to see what happens to the second number.

baff8802ebd1.text: Try addition, then multiplication, with the same two numbers.

179a67829d11.text: A two-operand percent experiment, not a complete Windows Calculator emulator.

28274972a8a2.text: Enable JavaScript to use the lab. The tutorial and reference results below remain readable.

97cf0ae66621.text: A two-operand percent experiment and a test matrix that checks intermediate state as well as the final answer.

3388dbb937b0.text: No setup for the lab. For binary inspection, use a Windows Calculator installation you can inspect and a configured native provider. The public Microsoft source provides an additional crosscheck.

d9e1ffa37f69.text: Ask a precise question: what happens when the user enters 200, chooses addition, enters 10, presses percent, then equals? Record the display after percent as well as after equals. The intermediate operand tells you more than the final answer alone.

7ada466d7e7a.text: This is standard-mode behavior. Keep mode, release and key sequence in the test record. Repeated equals, an omitted operand and a second percent press introduce additional state; leave those out of the first experiment.

cb0eedc65f6d.text: Investigate Windows Calculator standard-mode percentage behavior with REA. Compare the sequences 200 + 10 % = and 200 × 10 % =. Identify which installed module handles arithmetic, then trace the percent branch and operator-dependent operand transformation. Keep observed instructions, source interpretation and actual GUI input results separate.

d0741fb9b97f.text: 03. The launcher may not contain the calculation

4f84304f1e95.text: Opening a conveniently named executable is not enough. If it dispatches to another application, follow that handoff into the installed package. Record the file you actually analyzed and its hash.

8efd84e49313.text: In the upstream investigation, the arithmetic was in CalcViewModel.dll rather than the small calc.exe launcher. The report used analyst-assisted function selection. Its public Microsoft source reference helped interpret operator IDs; that reference was not proven to be the exact source commit of the installed binary.

136a407aaa32.text: Which file contains the arithmetic branch?

c7821ba0fac7.text: What selects percent, and what records the previous operator?

08825464f4b3.text: Where are the previous value and current entry stored?

38fa628e6068.text: Which arithmetic helpers are reached on each branch?

01f1b1b3da3e.text: For addition and subtraction, the entered percentage is relative to the first number. For multiplication and division, it becomes a fraction of 100. The pending operator is applied afterward. Keep those two stages separate in your implementation and in the interface.

1d05d65017c1.text: Our lab makes you press percent and equals separately so you can see that state change. Editing either input or switching operators starts a fresh sequence. It accepts two finite numbers, not an arbitrary calculator expression.

de1bd59a890f.text: Implement only this standard-mode two-operand percent behavior: + and − transform the entry to entry × (first / 100); × and ÷ transform it to entry / 100. Keep the transformed operand available for tests. Apply the pending operator only on equals. Handle division by zero, empty input and reset. Do not claim repeated-key or scientific-mode compatibility.

4e4e319f0ee5.text: 05. Test the intermediate value, not only the answer

6137ed230ff5.text: Two mistakes can sometimes cancel out and produce the expected final answer. Assert the transformed operand first, then the result. Include subtraction, division, zero and a negative first number so the test suite cannot pass by hardcoding the familiar addition example.

0cf02e37120e.text: If your fresh Windows run differs, check mode and exact input order before revising the formula. Save the key sequence and display states. The upstream report did not claim a completed original Windows GUI input check, so do not silently inherit one.

f6400c355356.text: Use these as explicit checkpoints. Matching them supports this small rule; it does not establish whole-application compatibility.

95e5d70895a5.text: Save both files in the same folder. Run the checks with Node.js; no package installation is needed.

c50af5d9cc3b.text: This site runs numeric tests against its own two-operand implementation, including the published Microsoft examples. It does not execute Microsoft’s test suite or automate the installed Windows application. Repeated percent, repeated equals, full expression parsing and scientific mode are outside the demo.

dbef1b19463a.text: 02. Connect to the version you can inspect

Read the loaded index.js. Find the initial speed, acceleration increment, update condition and speed threshold. Cite source locations. Do not rebuild the game yet.

Does it run on every render, only during play, or only when no collision occurs? Ask the agent to include the surrounding condition so the answer survives more than the happy path.

e975f372d714.text: The documented version starts at 6 and adds 0.001 on an eligible update if the current speed is below 13. That is not “0.001 per second.” Our teaching game uses 60 fixed logic updates per second; it draws independently of your display’s refresh rate.

6df2e7ac5b22.text: 04. Add a speed dial without losing the rule

2cc37d036b7c.text: Build the smallest game that makes the rule visible. Use a simple character, one obstacle, a jump button and a speed readout. The slider should switch to fixed speed; enabling automatic mode should return to the documented starting value.

9d8a7013e2dd.text: Do not silently replace the condition with a clamp to 13. That seems like a harmless cleanup, but it changes the result at the boundary. Keep the first implementation literal, then make intentional changes in a separate mode.

c258bcb93af5.text: Create an independent browser mini-game with Play/Pause, Jump and Restart. Reproduce only the documented speed update rule. Add a fixed-speed slider from 2 to 18 and an automatic mode starting at 6. Use a fixed logic timestep, pause offscreen, and allow keyboard and touch controls. Label new graphics, collision and jump behavior as teaching code. Test the imported speed function, not a second copy of it.

dd5e63e802d5.text: Run the speed function repeatedly without collisions. Compare the checkpoints below, keeping the unrounded value in the saved result. The surprising final value is the useful part of this exercise: a comparison happens before addition, and repeated floating-point increments need not land exactly on a decimal threshold.

46fe7ab5036d.text: If your result is 13.000 at 10,000 updates, check for a clamp or decimal rounding inside the loop. If it varies with screen refresh rate, check whether the simulation advances once per rendered frame.

3ae15379d944.text: Replay the actual acceleration function for 0, 1000, 4000, 7000 and 10000 updates from speed 6. Return full precision and three-decimal displays. aaf34d28db4f.text: 02. Follow the brick hit to the sound call

3a93ad1f3ee6.text: Start with a visible event: a brick breaks on one side of the screen. Work backward from the sound call and identify what value the caller passes. A number that looks like a coordinate could instead be a tile index, an offset or a scaled position.

0daf7fed0d33.text: Use the exact release identity in the upstream report before reusing its addresses. The reported target helper begins at 0x406400. If your executable differs, locate its corresponding behavior rather than assuming the same address works.

c92c93804061.text: Inspect my matching DX-Ball 1.07 executable with REA. Start from the pan helper identified in the official report and inspect its brick-hit caller. Explain how the caller constructs the argument. Cite both call-site instructions and the helper’s input load. Do not assume the decompiler signature is complete.

ded3019016c0.text: 03. When pseudocode loses the argument, read the instructions

6585d8a40d67.text: A decompiler can produce a short, unhelpful body even when the machine instructions are available. Inspect the stack load, floating-point operations, referenced data and integer conversion together. Ask for the original bytes of each constant, including its type and byte order.

017d97cee73f.text: The documented calculation is trunc((x × 1.5625 − 500) × scale). The caller supplies horizontal position. Notice the conversion at the end: truncation toward zero matters for negative values and is different from rounding down.

f04a16217ed2.text: Where does the input enter the function?

225afe13cc19.text: Which referenced bytes decode to each floating-point constant?

ede0cf74151a.text: Is scale a parameter, stored state or a fixed literal?

91961766f6d1.text: Does conversion truncate, round, saturate or overflow on the tested input range?

e657b58dc04c.text: First implement the numeric function and check left, center and right. Then add nearby positions that produce a fraction. At x = 319 and scale = 1, the raw value is −1.5625 and the integer result is −1. A floor operation would incorrectly produce −2.

527aebd4a05e.text: Our sound button maps pan / 500 into a Web Audio stereo panner and clamps that preview to −1…1. This makes direction easy to hear; it does not reproduce DirectSound’s volume curve or the original game audio. The displayed integer is not clamped.

09a753839a53.text: Implement the documented position-to-pan calculation independently. Test x = 0, 1, 319, 320, 321 and 640 at scales 0, 0.5, 1, 20 and −1. Preserve conversion toward zero. Build a user-triggered tone preview, label its normalization separately, and never use the preview’s clipping as the recovered numeric behavior.

22af18325754.text: The project reports comparing 641 integer positions with five scale settings against the original x86 function. It separately reports a 63-byte compiler match in its specified historical environment. Those are two different checks: matching behavior for selected inputs, and matching generated machine code.

a4dbe5ab5172.text: For your own investigation, retain each input pair and both outputs. If a mismatch appears, reduce it to the smallest failing case. Only attempt a byte match once the compiler version, options and relocation treatment are explicit. Our JavaScript tests cover the documented arithmetic; they do not repeat that original-binary comparison.

1ee929b32fd9.text: Get the executable’s address system right

ffd260f2a657.text: Recover one direction before drawing a ring

32fb3fadd732.text: Separate the ring rule from the aiming helper

ac1216a44747.text: Test the angles before judging the picture

5473b5793ecc.text: Drag the diamond around the center, then fire a ring. The pale ray marks the first bullet. Change the count from 16 to 12: integer angle steps no longer divide the circle evenly. Use the sliders if you prefer a keyboard.

47ea0eebfc23.text: Bullet ring. Drag the player diamond, or use the position sliders below.

70169f2e652b.text: Angle diagram, not game footage. Mouse aiming uses an approximate atan2 conversion; the original uses iatan2.

97d65de02089.text: The diagram runs immediately. To repeat binary inspection, use your own matching TH04 MAIN.EXE and a configured Ghidra provider. You also need the pinned reconstruction source linked below.

0ecca20c15f7.text: 02. Get the executable’s address system right

3e03436946b0.text: TH04 is a PC-98 DOS program. Before following a function address, establish how the loader maps the file into memory. Save the executable hash, load segment, code mode and address-to-file mapping with your notes. An address without its load profile can send you to the wrong bytes.

afb051802341.text: The official report provides a known helper and a pinned reconstruction to orient the investigation. Using that anchor is a guided exercise; it is not evidence that an agent discovered the entire program by itself.

599ffafd9c32.text: Use REA to open my TH04 MAIN.EXE with Ghidra. Verify the DOS MZ load profile and artifact identity against the linked TH04 evidence report. If they match, inspect the reported bullet_velocity_and_angle_set helper and map its address back to file bytes. If the artifact or load profile differs, stop using the historical addresses and explain how to locate an equivalent helper.

72b4c82f201e.text: 03. Recover one direction before drawing a ring

c8b4d9e1340e.text: The key question is the order of operations. Work through the index, count, aim and rotation separately. For this ring branch, the readable model is floor(index × 256 / count), plus the aim and rotation, wrapped into one byte. Angles increase clockwise on the screen.

71150b45ad4d.text: Try twelve bullets. Multiplying first and then dividing gives offsets 0, 21, 42, 64… Multiplying the index by floor(256 / count) would give 0, 21, 42, 63… Those paths agree initially, then drift. A visually plausible circle can hide the mistake.

196a6e87a449.text: REA Android Tutorial: Find Request Code in an APK

de0da8a4ed93.text: Analyze an Android APK with REA. Find request-building code, trace its callers, and separate candidate endpoints from observed network traffic.

27fff2a159ac.text: REA Android analysis: where does this APK send requests?

08b307f10282.text: Pick a single screen or action

eb9f83c7f855.text: Inspect the class, then select the method

7c288733b5db.text: Turn findings into a small specification

f4bbc1ff9c4b.text: An annotated chain from one feature to its request builder, with host, path and parameter candidates.

a2b2d6285384.text: An APK you can inspect, a full JDK 17+ and an existing jadx-headless-mcp 0.7.1 JAR. Check provider support for your host.

a6a90aa29c76.text: 01. Pick a single screen or action

776b446cb2bc.text: “List every API” is usually too broad. Start with a visible operation such as loading a public catalog. Note the APK version and the screen name. You want the code that builds that request, not every URL-shaped string in the package.

e169f87954fa.text: This is static inspection. The APK is not launched. Embedded strings can include abandoned hosts, test environments or paths that are combined with runtime configuration.

0313637778e2.text: Inspect /absolute/path/app.apk with REA. Locate the code for loading the public catalog. Trace from a likely screen or repository class to its networking method. Report host, path, HTTP method and parameter candidates with class and method evidence. Separate static declarations from confirmed runtime traffic.

f682b72fdef4.text: Use a full JDK, including its compiler module. Point REA at the provider JAR you already installed. If REA runs through your agent, configure the same environment for that server and restart it; setting a variable in a different terminal does not update an existing process.

abd29cbc6919.text: 03. Inspect the class, then select the method

b2cc0addf015.text: Class search matches class names, not arbitrary strings inside method bodies. Try feature names and common networking names such as Api, Service or Repository. Obfuscated packages may need a different entry point, such as a manifest activity followed into its dependencies.

7e3d31907028.text: Replace the class below with an exact name returned by search. Inspect its members before choosing a method. When overloaded methods share a name, use the overload index returned by the class inventory.

530860c71279.text: Read where the request is built and where the method is called. A constant base URL is only one piece: a builder can replace it, an interceptor can add parameters, and a native library can hide part of the process. Record each boundary.

e7c57db67298.text: Incoming references show static relationships known to the analysis engine. Reflection and dynamically loaded code can escape that set. If the result returns smali instead of Java, treat it as a different representation of the same method and inspect it explicitly.

4f970a317f10.text: Which caller connects this method to the chosen feature?

cf042ff4b269.text: Is the base URL a literal, resource, configuration value or runtime result?

39382f665fec.text: Which fields are actually added to the request?

4b694bb71c6e.text: Where does the static trace stop?

c6269e658889.text: 05. Turn findings into a small specification

e2af89f05939.text: Write a table containing the candidate method, URL construction, parameter names and supporting method references. Leave runtime-only values unknown. Use a local mock server to prototype your own client against this specification.

5fc19e833ec4.text: Do not count a static endpoint list as a successful request capture. To make that claim, you need a separately recorded run of the matching app version in an appropriate test environment. This tutorial supplies the inspection workflow; it does not claim a tested APK or a captured API response.

1113d6396cfd.text: No request? Inspect the client-side path

ce3c8b0ddd75.text: 03. Record a baseline, then one export

0288ea51c680.text: First record a short idle window so background polling is visible. Then start a second observation and click Export yourself while the window is open. REA’s passive observer does not click the button for you.

7068b3265f5c.text: Keep the input small and recognizable, such as two rows with a unique test label. Note whether the app shows a spinner, downloads a file or reports an error. Compare the two captures rather than assuming every new request belongs to Export.

7a146739ac34.text: Does a request begin after the action?

f128f6bf45b4.text: What are its method, URL and reported status?

0a4a74e33695.text: The bundle analysis reports static candidates. A string resembling an endpoint is not proof it was called. Keep request observations and source findings in separate columns.

dde23a664f99.text: REA Version Comparison: Investigate an Electron Update

3b47125b3589.text: Compare two Electron releases with REA. Find the code change behind a broken workflow, replay the same input, and build a focused regression test.

6240715ecaaf.text: REA version comparison: what did the update change?

673089c1193e.text: Compare the feature, not the minified names

26304bb8e7fe.text: Replay the same input in both versions

63461bb3ff5b.text: A focused change report with artifact identities, source evidence and a repeatable before/after check.

dc374204a906.text: Both releases of an app you can inspect, their ASAR archives or extracted folders, and REA 6.4.0.

82e1b7641f50.text: “The update broke export” leaves too much room for guesses. Write down the input, the action and the difference: for example, a title containing a quotation mark exported correctly before the update and now produces a malformed CSV row.

03d1e0598019.text: Put the two application versions in separate folders. Record their release labels and artifact hashes. Compare equivalent artifacts: a development source tree and a production minified bundle are not the same kind of evidence.

be444e8a233b.text: Keep the complete original JSON outputs. The comparison workflow expects authenticated application evidence; a manually edited summary or a list of filenames is not a substitute.

ca0826ce95e1.text: Ask your connected agent to inspect the available compare_application_versions schema and supply the two results accordingly. This avoids guessing nested input fields that may change between releases. The CLI can show the same contract.

6a2d95fd30de.text: Use REA compare_application_versions with the complete application evidence in before.json and after.json. Check the installed tool schema first. Focus the report on CSV export: changed modules, related call paths and unresolved matches. Do not interpret a missing node in partial coverage as proof of deletion.

5cc8f07ca0e7.text: 03. Compare the feature, not the minified names

1800a232314a.text: Start at the button, IPC channel or formatter you already know. Follow that feature in both versions and inspect the changed code. Minified variable names often change during a rebuild without changing behavior.

76adc59151c1.text: A module digest can establish exact identity. A renamed function or a newly numbered bundle chunk cannot establish a semantic change by itself. Keep unmatched or partially parsed regions visible in the report.

af29568cf591.text: Do both versions contain the relevant feature entry?

7338ddadd4e4.text: Does the changed branch affect the failing input?

2f3b60c3c236.text: Could packaging, configuration or missing coverage explain the difference?

66e3fdde5076.text: 04. Replay the same input in both versions

df23c396a8c9.text: Use separate disposable data folders so opening the newer app does not migrate the older version’s test state. Run exactly the same operation against the same test content. Save the output file or a focused behavior record from each run.

4f4d193f48bd.text: For a CSV regression, parse the resulting rows and compare fields. Byte differences such as line endings can matter, but a changed timestamp should not drown out the actual quoting failure. Document every normalization used in the comparison.

4ffcc08ccfc7.text: Create a regression test for the exact input we observed. Compare parsed exported fields from the old and new output. Show both the raw difference and any normalized comparison. Keep the suspected source change separate from the behavior actually reproduced.

158c24924194.text: Include the two version identities, one failing input, exact reproduction steps, observed old/new outputs and the smallest relevant source difference. State whether the behavior was reproduced or only predicted from static code.

18eee0a8a9d9.text: A good comparison gives you a next action: a regression test, a compatibility workaround or a narrowly scoped replacement. This tutorial is a workflow; it does not claim a regression in a named commercial release.

ae2bfcf0c78f.text: REA Electron Tutorial: Trace Notion’s Clipboard

cf19143c815e.text: Use REA to follow Notion’s reported clipboard path, from the renderer through IPC to the system clipboard. Apply the method to your own Electron app.

e5ffd4144240.text: Notion: how does an Electron app copy rich text?

e0d67d8ccf28.text: Start with the payload, not the whole app

3bcdf1d505c7.text: When the trace stops at a wrapper

3b18c0fdce76.text: A source-backed map of the text and HTML payload, the process boundary and the clipboard writer.

bc166d544035.text: REA, an Electron app you can inspect, and its app.asar or extracted JavaScript. No native engine is needed.

f9e4e41ba0aa.text: 01. Start with the payload, not the whole app

1f7667b635b9.text: Copying bold text feels like one operation. In Electron, the editor, the bridge exposed to a web page, and the process allowed to write to the operating system may be different pieces of code. Your job is to connect them.

1319aaa67e6b.text: The official Notion investigation followed Desktop 7.6.1. Its reported route passes text and HTML through a clipboard API and an IPC receiver. The graph alone did not resolve the entire route: direct reading of wrapper code supplied missing links. This tutorial applies that investigation method; it is not a new capture of Notion.

bf475422b942.text: Use REA to inspect /absolute/path/app.asar. Investigate only copying rich text. Find the renderer call, preload bridge, IPC channel, receiving handler and final clipboard write. For each link, show its file and source range. Mark dynamic or missing links as unresolved. Do not run the application.

c7fc942ce5dc.text: Work on a copy of the application files. On macOS, Electron packages often put app.asar under Contents/Resources; Windows and Linux packages commonly use a resources folder. Confirm the path instead of assuming every application uses the same layout.

7f62a1d51e4f.text: Keep any app.asar.unpacked companion directory beside the archive. Review parse failures, skipped files and the discovered main entry before trusting the map. An incomplete inventory can hide the receiver you need.

83c829107cad.text: Ask the agent to inspect the actual source around contextBridge, clipboard and ipcRenderer.invoke references returned by the analysis. A bridge may expose a generic function whose channel is passed through a variable. Searching the graph for the literal channel can return nothing even when the wrapper source contains it.

d22117a08d74.text: The upstream Notion report identified the channel notion:clipboard:write by reading the packaged API object, then connected its receiver to Electron clipboard.write. Record the equivalent names from your own version; do not paste historical offsets into a different release.

b167f56cb6e2.text: Renderer: which event constructs the copy payload?

e70938d9c04f.text: Preload: which public API forwards it, and how is the channel supplied?

0c54e74c6bfa.text: Main process: which handler receives it, and how is the sender checked?

ee7457381f54.text: Sink: which text, HTML or custom fields reach the clipboard API?

b99f11162082.text: In a disposable document, copy a short sentence containing one bold word. Paste it into a rich-text editor and a plain-text editor. Record both outputs. Repeat with a link, a line break and non-ASCII characters. These checks distinguish plain text fallback from preserved formatting.

78558f1079c2.text: A matching source route does not prove that your operating system accepted every format. The upstream investigation also used separately cached web modules; it did not record a same-version desktop copy session. Keep that distinction in your own report.

0c1c73e1386b.text: Build a small copy-payload function for my own app using the behavior we established. Keep plain text and HTML separate. Add tests for bold text, links, line breaks and Unicode. List any custom clipboard formats that remain unexplained; do not claim full Notion compatibility.

c2b015db1b74.text: 05. When the trace stops at a wrapper

32f7e7dcb3c4.text: Inspect the wrapper definition and its call site together. If a channel name is assembled at runtime, record the expression rather than inventing a literal value. If a native addon performs the write, the JavaScript analysis ends at that boundary.

83a94cda75df.text: A local executable you can inspect and a configured native analysis provider such as Ghidra. The commands below explicitly select Ghidra.

67e6d9d53a4a.text: 01. Use the error as your entry point

b0cd6c948733.text: An application refuses a file. Its interface says “File too large”, but does that mean bytes, decoded pixels, compressed size or a service limit? Recover the decision before changing your own implementation.

33ec7b7cc5f7.text: Choose one exact message from your target. Search the native engine’s analyzed strings. A missing result does not prove the message is absent: it may be localized, encoded, assembled at runtime or stored outside the executable.

eebc824e9352.text: 02. Find the function that uses the string

b69e7af30520.text: Take the address from the search result and inspect its references. A reference may point to a general error-display helper rather than the actual guard. Follow the caller until you find the branch deciding whether to report the error.

2e941de05ef8.text: The placeholders below must be replaced with addresses returned for your binary. Addresses from another build are not interchangeable.

aec6d9d5fa3b.text: 03. Recover the comparison, including its units

99be46dc589b.text: Identify both sides of the comparison. Follow where the size value comes from, whether arithmetic happens before the comparison, and whether the branch uses greater-than or greater-than-or-equal. Those details decide the edge case.

505e0fd82d5c.text: Treat decompiled names and types as working hypotheses. If the result is incomplete, inspect the selected function’s instructions and callees. Signedness, integer width and conversion order can change the result even when the pseudocode looks simple.

1a16537b0eaf.text: Use the returned function evidence to explain the branch that emits this error. Trace the compared value back to its input. Identify the threshold, units, signedness and exact comparison. If decompilation is incomplete, inspect instructions and the relevant helper. Cite addresses and mark unresolved types instead of guessing.

b2ce18e2a7a6.text: 04. Probe the boundary, not just a happy path

3fee27190796.text: If the recovered rule uses a threshold L, test L−1, L and L+1 in the input’s actual units. Also test zero and malformed input where the application accepts it. Run these only in your controlled copy of the program.

94683cf19e44.text: For a file-size guard, record file bytes and the observed outcome. For a decoded-image guard, varying file bytes alone may not exercise the relevant condition. Compare the same input with your replacement and save mismatches.

e18fe251630e.text: Does malformed input fail earlier in a different branch?

96d8e7d222ac.text: 05. Keep the conclusion the size of the evidence

2228eaeb5c1b.text: Your deliverable is one recovered rule and the tests run against it. This workflow has not been executed on a particular target for this article; the error text is a scenario to replace with your own.

2e7604b1f4f6.text: For a real example of the same discipline, the REA project documents DX-Ball’s sound-pan function: its report distinguishes 3,205 differential input checks from a separate 63-byte compiler match. Neither claim means the whole game is reconstructed. See the linked official native guide and its case study for that investigation.
